title: Pennsylvania's 6th Congressional District election, 2026
jurisdiction: Pennsylvania's 6th Congressional District (Chester County and part of Berks County)
description: The 2026 election for Pennsylvania's 6th Congressional District pits four-term Democratic incumbent Chrissy Houlahan against Republican challenger Marty Young. The district encompasses all of Chester County and part of Berks County in the Philadelphia suburbs, an area that has trended Democratic in recent years. Houlahan, an Air Force veteran and former engineer and educator, emphasizes her record on national security, health care access, and government accountability. Young, a West Point graduate, Army National Guard officer, and corporate restructuring executive, is running on a platform of fiscal discipline, cutting government waste, and what he describes as common-sense conservative solutions. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid D,' and the primary elections were held on May 19, 2026.
polling_note: No traditional public opinion polls were found for this race. Cook Political Report rates PA-06 as 'Solid Democratic.' Prediction markets favor Houlahan heavily (97% chance of Democratic win per City & State PA).

candidates.name: Chrissy Houlahan
candidates.summary: Chrissy Houlahan is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. She is an Air Force veteran, engineer, entrepreneur, and former educator who serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. Houlahan emphasizes her work on national security, health care affordability, gun safety, and government transparency.

candidates.name: Marty Young
candidates.summary: Marty Young is the Republican nominee for Pennsylvania's 6th Congressional District, having won the May 19, 2026 primary. He is a U.S. Army veteran (Infantry Officer and Chaplain), currently serving as a Lieutenant Colonel in the Army National Guard, and a corporate restructuring executive. Young emphasizes his military service, business leadership in stabilizing struggling companies, and a platform focused on fiscal responsibility, health care reform, and cutting government waste.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polls exist for this race, so the forecast relies entirely on non-polling indicators. Chrissy Houlahan is a four-term Democratic incumbent in a Philadelphia-suburban district (Chester County and part of Berks County) that has trended Democratic in recent cycles. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid D.' Prediction markets heavily favor a Democratic win (~97% per City & State PA). The challenger, Marty Young, is a credible Republican candidate (West Point graduate, Army National Guard officer, corporate executive) but faces steep headwinds in a district that has consistently elected Houlahan by double-digit margins since 2018. The absence of any traditional polling data reduces confidence from high to medium, but the structural and contextual signals strongly support a safe Democratic hold.
